create.name: Sanshin Zen Community / Sanshinji
create.bio:
Sanshin Zen Community is a Soto Zen temple, Sanshinji, in Bloomington, Indiana. It was founded by Shohaku Okumura, a Japanese priest ordained by Kosho Uchiyama in 1970 and long occupied with putting Dogen's writings into English, and it keeps the style of practice handed from Kodo Sawaki to Uchiyama and on to Okumura. Okumura handed over the running of the temple in 2023; his dharma heir Hoko Karnegis, who holds an international teaching appointment from the Soto school in Japan, now guides the sangha alongside a circle of ordained and lay practice leaders.

The community's life rests on four strands: zazen, shared work on the temple and grounds, close study of Dogen and the lineage texts, and ritual. Sitting is held on weekday mornings, Wednesday evenings and Sunday mornings, when a dharma talk follows, and most periods can be joined on Zoom. Its hallmark is the silent sesshin of Uchiyama's Antaiji, days given almost entirely to zazen with no talks or interviews, held several times a year, together with an annual precepts retreat and free Getting Started evenings for newcomers. A companion website, Sanshin Source, and a YouTube archive of several hundred talks carry the teaching further afield.

courses.title: Rohatsu Sesshin
courses.description: Seven days of silent sitting marking the Buddha's awakening, run on the temple's simple sesshin timetable from five in the morning to eight at night with formal oryoki meals. Whole-sesshin or selected full days can be booked in person, and the zazen periods are open to drop in on Zoom.
courses.price: Base $520 or $65/day; sponsor $648 or $81/day; or offer what you can

courses.title: Getting Started in Zen Practice
courses.description: A free evening session held twice a month, one in the zendo and one on Zoom, introducing zazen, the body and breath in sitting, and the basics of Buddhist and Zen teaching, with time for questions. It can be attended once or repeatedly, and newcomers register in advance.

courses.title: Precepts Retreat
courses.description: A five-day residential retreat studying the sixteen bodhisattva precepts through zazen, talks by the preceptor, discussion, work and silent meals, ending with a public jukai ceremony. Those receiving the precepts apply in advance and also attend two rakusu sewing retreats in the spring.

free_resources.title: Virtual Practice with Sanshin
free_resources.description: Weekday morning zazen and service, Wednesday evening sitting and book discussion, and Sunday zazen with a dharma talk, all open to join on Zoom from this page, with the chant book to download.

free_resources.title: Sanshin Source
free_resources.description: The community's companion library of essays, talks and study notes on Soto Zen doctrine, zazen, ritual, precepts, lineage and the Sanshin style of sesshin, open to anyone.
